مَنْكَصٌ , (O, B, K,) like مَقْعَدٌ, (TA,) [in the CK, erroneously, مُنَكَّص,] A place to which one removes, withdraws, or retires afar off, syn. مُتَنَحًّى. (O, B, K.) El-Aashà says, praising 'Alkamah Ibn-'Olátheh, “أَعَلْقَمُ قَدْ جَبَرَتْنِى الأُمُورُ
إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كَانَ لِى مَنْكَصُ
” [O 'Alkamah, affairs have compelled me to have recourse to thee, and there was not for me any place to which to retire. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
